solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Search of fort I twice organised? It's regularly screened

indicators.note: organised means put into a new arrangement, so the letters before it are rearranged
twice asks for the letter I to be written two times over

explanation.surface: Someone methodically combs through a fort, and the result is something shown again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles the I, giving the fourteen letters SEARCHOFFORTII that 'organised' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1981 Oscar-winning film about Olympic runners is shown on television over and over, so it is regularly screened.

clue.text: Elaborate dish cooked backstage at rep

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or falsified, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fancy meal is prepared behind the scenes at a repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BACKSTAGEATREP; 'rep' looks like a theatre company but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rich dish of beef steak stuffed with oysters, so it is a suitably elaborate preparation.

clue.text: J Stewart's contemporary occupying office, one offering illumination?

parts.note: the film actor Alan Ladd, a Hollywood contemporary of James Stewart, written as initial and surname, A Ladd
a party occupying office is in, that is in power

explanation.surface: An actor of James Stewart's era holds public office and brings enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is given as an initial plus surname: A for Alan, then LADD.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime hero owns the magic lamp, so playfully he is someone who provides light.

clue.text: Opera showing excited patriot lacking power and lover

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order
lacking means going without, so one letter is taken out of the word patriot

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An opera depicts a fervent patriot who has neither influence nor a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from PATRIOT to leave ATRIOT; 'excited' then rearranges ATRIOT with LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's 1853 work about a troubadour is one of the best-known Italian operas.

clue.text: African bird in a court fluttering

indicators.note: fluttering means flapping about, so the letters of a court are jumbled

explanation.surface: An African bird flits about inside a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges ACOURT.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly coloured plantain-eater lives in the forests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa.

clue.text: Musical composition a high point among many in stellar group

indicators.note: among means placed amid, so the first pieces are set inside the constellation's name
the clue's 'many in stellar group' is read as the letter for many being dropped from the constellation, a loose signal

parts.note: Orion is a constellation, a group of stars
N stands for an indefinite large number, as in 'to the nth degree'
a tor is a rocky peak, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A piece of music celebrates a lofty summit set among a great cluster of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the insertion, but nothing clean signals dropping the letter for 'many' from the constellation; the blog reads it the same loose way. A tor is a rocky hill in England's West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred work for voices and orchestra, such as Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Some animals in distance (long gone)

definitions.note: furred animals collectively, a plural sense

indicators.note: gone means departed, so the word long is taken away from the distance

parts.note: a furlong is a distance of an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing

explanation.surface: Certain animals are far away, long since vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(long gone)' tells you to remove LONG from FURLONG, not that the animals are extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries list furred animals taken as a group as one sense, as in 'fur and feather'.

clue.text: Band around Greek character mostly involved in disorder?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the band encloses the shortened letter

parts.note: a ring is a band, as of metal worn on a finger

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the Greek letter is dropped

parts.note: iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A musical band surrounds a Greek figure who is largely caught up in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it means a circular band. 'mostly' drops the Greek letter's last letter, and 'around' wraps the band round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: People taking part in a riot are engaged in a public disturbance, hence the question mark for a participle.

clue.text: A round venue after course?

parts.note: a golf course has eighteen holes, and golfers then gather for a round of drinks at the clubhouse bar, jokingly named as the next hole

explanation.surface: A circular place to visit once a course is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' and 'course' suggest a meal or studies; here they are a round of drinks and a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar where drinks are bought after eighteen holes have been played.

clue.text: Priest taken around a nuclear facility

indicators.note: taken around means the priest is wrapped about the next letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clergyman is shown round a nuclear power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken around' puts the priest outside A.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the plant where controlled nuclear fission takes place.

clue.text: One in charge of order engaged in fine reasoning

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied inside, so the head of the order sits within the two characters for fine

parts.note: A1 means first-class or fine, written here as A and the letter I for 1
a prior heads a religious order or priory

explanation.surface: A monastic superior takes part in some excellent argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, Lloyd's register mark for first-rate, has its 1 read as the letter I; 'engaged in' places PRIOR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes deduction from known principles rather than from experience, a mode of reasoning.

clue.text: Sign of flexibility book exposed? That's the object

indicators.note: exposed means stripped bare, here taking the book's letter off the front

parts.note: a bend shows that something is flexible

explanation.surface: A book with a bending spine is laid open to reveal its purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips B from the front of BEND.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or goal, as in 'a means to an end', so it is the object of an action.

clue.text: Side on pitch clued in and on form? I'm elated!

parts.note: on, the leg side of a cricket field, is one side of the pitch

indicators.note: form is taken as a verb, to shape, so these letters are moulded into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A cricket team, briefed and in good form, has a player exclaiming his delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON side is the leg side in cricket. 'form' rearranges CLUEDINON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blissfully happy is the idiom's meaning, so the exclamation stands for the state of the speaker.

clue.text: Places for swimmers? Hold a pair in ground

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, meaning crushed, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A pair of swimmers are kept inside an enclosure of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for land but is the past of grind; it rearranges HOLDAPAIRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: These are aquarium pools where dolphins are kept and displayed, so homes for swimming creatures.

clue.text: Diet followed by a male, small one

indicators.note: followed by means the diet comes first and the rest after it

parts.note: to bant is to diet, after William Banting's slimming regime

explanation.surface: A slimming diet, and then a man, makes for a little person.
explanation.walkthrough: BANT is an old verb for slimming, from Banting's 1860s diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of fowl, and the word is used for anything diminutive.

clue.text: Dreary record heard in conversation

indicators.note: heard tells you the following answer comes from words spoken out loud

parts.note: dire means dreary or dismal; a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A tedious diary entry is overheard during a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, 'dire log' matches the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is an exchange of talk between two or more people.

clue.text: Bird is a decoration sitting in sporty car with volunteers

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside, so the honour sits within the car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sporty car
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A medal-winner rides in a fast car alongside some volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting in' signals the container. The decoration is a British honour; the volunteers are the Territorial Army, Britain's former part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambetta is an old name for the redshank, a wading bird.

clue.text: See in part of Ireland horse

indicators.note: in places the exclamation inside the county name

parts.note: Galway is a county and city in the west of Ireland
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Look at a horse in a corner of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as a verb but supplies the old exclamation meaning look, which 'in' places inside the name of a western Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: A Galloway is a small sturdy breed of horse from south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Dimwit, desperate sort taken in by enticement

indicators.note: taken in by means swallowed up, so the character is placed inside the enticement

parts.note: a lure is a bait or enticement
Desperate Dan is the strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A foolish person, at the end of their tether, falls for a temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate sort' points to Desperate Dan, the strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a lazy or stupid person, so a fair synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Small house captured by outlaw in kingdom

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the hut sits within the outlaw word

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a hut is a small, simple dwelling

explanation.surface: A cottage is seized by a bandit somewhere in a realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit but is the verb BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan state is a constitutional monarchy, ruled by the Dragon King.

clue.text: Disciplined in trade — like a good apprentice?

indicators.note: disciplined means drilled into order, so the letters of in trade are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone schooled in a craft behaves as a model apprentice should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disciplined' looks like the definition, but it is the anagram signal for INTRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A good apprentice ends up skilled through instruction, so this adjective describes one.

clue.text: Island cut plant in orderly system

parts.note: Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Greek island

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the plant loses its final letter

parts.note: moss is a small flowerless plant

explanation.surface: An island's trimmed plants are arranged in a tidy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' tempts as the definition, since the answer is also a garden flower, but 'in' links to the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe seen as an ordered, harmonious whole is the Greek-derived sense, opposite of chaos.

clue.text: Short walk around essential feature of hill revealing mayfly

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the short walk wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a turn is a short stroll, as in 'take a turn round the garden'
key means essential or crucial
the brow is the top or edge of a hill

explanation.surface: A brief stroll round the main part of a hillside turns up an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential feature of hill' looks like one phrase but is two pieces, KEY and BROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of upwinged insect, also an artificial fly of that name used by anglers.

clue.text: Rule ignored in spots remains

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter for rule is removed

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
R stands for rule, as in R for rex or regina

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule leaves something behind in the pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes R from RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left after burning is the powdery residue of a fire, the leftovers of combustion.

clue.text: Obdurate old musical artist

definitions.meaning: obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind
... was a British pop star of the early 1980s

explanation.surface: A stubborn veteran performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Ant fronted the 1980s British band Adam and the Ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding in opinion fits the adjective; the second sense is the pop singer's stage name.

clue.text: Support shown during maiden

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the word maiden

explanation.surface: Help is offered in the course of a girl's first outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' points inside MAIDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and support are synonyms for help or assistance.

clue.text: Horse followed with new success? Noted one

indicators.note: followed with means the horse comes first, then the other pieces

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a go is a success, as in 'make a go of it'

explanation.surface: A horse goes on to fresh victory and becomes famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is short: 'Noted one' means a famous horse, linked to the 'Horse' at the start; the battle that gave the horse its name was itself a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's grey charger, named after his 1800 victory, is the most famous horse in history.

clue.text: Stiff feel about second security device

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two words together enclose the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead man
to handle is to feel or touch

explanation.surface: A rigid sense of touch for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective but is slang for a corpse; 'about' makes the two outer words together surround the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: On trains a control must be held by the driver or the brakes apply, a safety mechanism.
